issues.label: Certiorari jurisdiction and scope
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction and define the questions presented and record limits on certiorari review.

issues.label: Standard of review: suppression
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standards for factual findings, legal conclusions, and mixed questions in an identification-suppression ruling.

issues.label: Standard of review: ICA decision
issues.why: The court must determine how to review the ICA’s reasoning and remedy (vacatur/remand) for legal error.

issues.label: Preservation of issues
issues.why: The court must decide whether the State’s and defendant’s arguments were preserved below and properly raised on appeal/certiorari.

issues.label: Kaneaiakala governing framework
issues.why: The court must apply State v. Kaneaiakala’s two-step due process analysis for suggestive identifications and reliability.

issues.label: Constitutional basis of exclusion
issues.why: The court must identify whether exclusion is grounded in Hawaiʻi due process, federal due process, or both, affecting analysis and remedy.

issues.label: Suggestiveness of show-up
issues.why: The court must decide whether the field show-up was impermissibly suggestive under the totality of circumstances.

issues.label: One-person show-up procedure
issues.why: The court must assess inherent suggestiveness and whether exigency/necessity justified a one-person show-up rather than a lineup.

issues.label: Handcuffs and custody cues
issues.why: The court must evaluate the impact of the defendant being handcuffed with an officer positioned behind him on suggestiveness.

issues.label: Police statements about custody
issues.why: The court must assess whether telling CW police “had a male in custody” improperly conveyed that the suspect was present.

issues.label: Failure to give non-suspect warning
issues.why: The court must consider the effect of not warning that the perpetrator may or may not be present, especially due to language barrier.

issues.label: Language/interpretation adequacy
issues.why: The court must consider whether lack of a Chuukese interpreter undermined the fairness of the procedure and the reliability assessment.

issues.label: Use of family member interpreter
issues.why: The court must consider whether using CW’s granddaughter earlier (and not during the show-up) affects accuracy, contamination, or procedural fairness.

issues.label: Ambulance reroute circumstances
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether rerouting the ambulance for identification created pressure or implied urgency affecting reliability.

issues.label: Medical condition and stress
issues.why: The court must account for CW’s injuries, pain, age, stress, and medical transport context when assessing identification reliability.

issues.label: Opportunity to view assailant
issues.why: The court must evaluate CW’s viewing conditions during the assault (duration, distance, lighting, attention) for reliability.

issues.label: Time between crime and show-up
issues.why: The court must consider the short interval’s effect on memory accuracy and whether it offsets or is overwhelmed by suggestiveness.

issues.label: Accuracy of prior description
issues.why: The court must consider what description CW gave before the show-up and whether it matched Jercy, despite no written statement.

issues.label: Documentation of description
issues.why: The court must consider whether the lack of a contemporaneous written statement affects the weight/reliability assessment or admissibility.

issues.label: Cross-racial/ethnic identification
issues.why: The court must consider whether cross-racial or cross-ethnic factors bear on reliability under HAWJIC 3.19.

issues.label: Witness capacity to identify
issues.why: The court must assess CW’s vision, attention, cognitive capacity, and communication limitations in the identification context.

issues.label: Witness certainty and basis
issues.why: The court must consider CW’s level of certainty and whether it reflects her recollection rather than suggestive reinforcement.

issues.label: Post-identification feedback risk
issues.why: The court must consider whether officers’ or neighbors’ conduct after identification could inflate confidence or contaminate memory.

issues.label: Other persons not shown
issues.why: The court must consider the effect of not presenting fillers or alternative suspects on suggestiveness and reliability.

issues.label: Role of neighbors’ detention
issues.why: The court must consider whether neighbors’ belief and detention of Jercy influenced the identification process or conveyed suspect status to CW.

issues.label: Independent source for in-court ID
issues.why: If the show-up is excluded, the court must decide whether any in-court identification has an independent reliable basis.

issues.label: Admissibility vs weight distinction
issues.why: The court must distinguish between suppression (legal admissibility) and leaving issues to the jury (weight) under Kaneaiakala.

issues.label: Required findings on factors
issues.why: The court must decide whether the trial court must expressly address HAWJIC 3.19A factors in written/oral findings or may implicitly consider them.

issues.label: Sufficiency of trial court analysis
issues.why: The court must determine whether the circuit court actually considered show-up suggestiveness factors and their effect on reliability.

issues.label: ICA’s interpretation of Kaneaiakala
issues.why: The court must decide whether the ICA correctly applied Kaneaiakala in requiring specific factor consideration and in evaluating reliability.

issues.label: Totality-of-circumstances application
issues.why: The court must ensure the correct holistic balancing of reliability factors against suggestiveness rather than a checklist approach.

issues.label: Burden of proof on admissibility
issues.why: The court must confirm which party bears what burden to show suggestiveness and/or reliability under Hawaiʻi law post-Kaneaiakala.

issues.label: Record adequacy for review
issues.why: The court must decide whether the record allows appellate review of the identification procedure given translation gaps and limited documentation.

issues.label: Remedy for suppression error
issues.why: The court must decide whether the appropriate remedy is vacatur/new trial, limited remand for findings, or affirmance.

issues.label: Harmless error analysis
issues.why: The court must determine whether any erroneous admission of the identification was harmless beyond a reasonable doubt.

issues.label: Harmless error: other evidence
issues.why: The court must assess the strength of non-identification evidence (neighbors’ pursuit/detention, proximity, etc.) and whether it independently proves identity.

issues.label: Neighbors’ identification limits
issues.why: The court must consider that Hernandez lost sight briefly and Wainit lacked a clear view, affecting whether their testimony supports harmlessness.

issues.label: Prosecutorial use of ID at trial
issues.why: The court must consider how heavily the State relied on the show-up identification in arguments and whether it impacted the verdict.

issues.label: Jury instruction considerations
issues.why: The court must consider whether HAWJIC 3.19/3.19A (or equivalents) were given and whether instruction adequacy affects prejudice/harmlessness.

issues.label: Second-degree assault elements
issues.why: The court must ensure the charged subsection’s elements (including victim age requirement, injury/intent if applicable) were properly supported and instructed, as they intersect with identification significance.

issues.label: Due process fairness overall
issues.why: The court must consider whether the identification procedure, viewed overall, created a substantial likelihood of misidentification requiring exclusion.

issues.label: Limits on appellate factfinding
issues.why: The court must avoid substituting its own fact determinations for the trial court’s credibility and factual findings in the suppression context.

issues.label: Effect of missing interpreter instruction
issues.why: The court must consider whether inability to instruct CW about the procedure is itself a suggestive factor increasing misidentification risk.

issues.label: Potential cumulative error
issues.why: If multiple identification-related errors occurred (procedure, findings, instructions), the court must assess their combined prejudice.
